description: Deterministic message generation and validation oracle shared byte-for-byte between the Java and Rust suites. Every sender variant writes the same 16-byte header (sequence, payloadLength, both little-endian u64) + deterministic payload wire format to a TCP loopback connection; the receiver validates every message and reports how many were delivered.

headerPlusPayload.note: The representative case: a small fixed header, a meaningfully-sized payload.

smallMessages.note: Payload barely larger than the header itself — per-message fixed overhead dominates here.

mixedSizes.note: Payload size cycles through this list — exercises the wire format's variable-length payload support; each message's header still records its own exact payloadLength.

wireFormat: header: bytes[0..8) = sequence (LE u64), bytes[8..16) = payloadLength (LE u64); payload: payload[i] = (sequence + i) & 0xFF for i in [0, payloadLength)

writeAccounting.note: writeCalls counts application-level write()/write_vectored() invocations — an honest proxy for kernel crossings, never a verified syscall count (see the 'counting application calls instead of syscalls' trap). Real syscall counts require strace on the native-Linux evidence host.
